summary: Reviewed the dvpwa (sqli) aiohttp application: DAO layer, views, middlewares, auth utilities, Jinja2 setup, config and templates. The application contains multiple high-impact, reachable vulnerabilities including an unauthenticated SQL injection, application-wide disabled HTML autoescaping leading to stored XSS, weak unsalted MD5 password hashing, disabled CSRF protection, and a session cookie without HttpOnly. Overall risk is critical: an unauthenticated attacker can execute arbitrary SQL and persist XSS that steals sessions. Coverage is the full Python package and templates; static third-party JS/CSS assets were not audited.

findings.title: Unauthenticated SQL injection in Student.create
findings.description: Student.create builds an INSERT statement by interpolating the raw 'name' value into the SQL string with Python %-formatting instead of using a parameterized query. The value flows unmodified from the POST body: views.students() (sqli/views.py:54-57) calls Student.create(conn, data['name']) on any POST to /students/. The route (sqli/routes.py:14) has no authentication and the CSRF middleware is disabled (see separate finding), so any anonymous internet user can inject arbitrary SQL. Because the value is wrapped in single quotes, an attacker submits name=x'); DROP TABLE marks;-- or a stacked/boolean payload to read or modify any data, or use PostgreSQL features to escalate. This is the only string-formatted query in the DAO layer; all other DAO methods correctly use bound parameters.
findings.evidence:
q = ("INSERT INTO students (name) "
     "VALUES ('%(name)s')" % {'name': name})
...
await cur.execute(q)   # name comes from request.post()['name'] in views.students (views.py:57), unauthenticated POST /students/
findings.recommendation: Use a parameterized query and let the driver bind the value, e.g. await cur.execute("INSERT INTO students (name) VALUES (%(name)s)", {'name': name}) with no surrounding quotes and no %-formatting of the SQL string.

findings.title: Stored XSS via application-wide disabled Jinja2 autoescape
findings.description: aiohttp_jinja2 is configured with autoescape=False, so every template expression that does not explicitly pipe through | e renders raw HTML. Multiple templates print attacker-controlled, database-stored values without escaping, producing stored XSS. Reachable sinks include review.review_text (sqli/templates/course.jinja2:22) which is submitted via POST /courses/{id}/review with no authentication (views.review, views.py:111-131), course.title and course.description (course.jinja2:14-15, student.jinja2:19-20), and student.name (students.jinja2:16, course.jinja2:49). An anonymous user posts a review containing <script>...</script>; it executes in every visitor's browser, including admins, and combined with the non-HttpOnly session cookie allows session hijacking. Root cause is the single autoescape=False setting; fixing it re-enables escaping across all templates.
findings.evidence:
sqli/app.py:33-35 setup_jinja(app, loader=..., context_processors=[...], autoescape=False)
Sinks: course.jinja2:22 {{ review.review_text }}; course.jinja2:14 {{ course.title }}; course.jinja2:15 {{ course.description }}; students.jinja2:16 {{ name }}; course.jinja2:49 {{ student.name }}. Source: views.review -> Review.create(conn, course_id, review_text) with review_text=request.post()['review_text'].
findings.recommendation: Set autoescape=True (or autoescape=select_autoescape(['jinja2','html'])) in setup_jinja and remove the now-redundant | e filters, or at minimum escape every user-controlled variable. Enabling autoescape globally is the correct fix.

findings.title: Weak unsalted MD5 password hashing in User.check_password
findings.description: Passwords are verified (and, per migrations/001-fixtures.sql:10-13, stored) as unsalted MD5 hashes. MD5 is fast and unsalted, so any leaked pwd_hash (e.g. via the SQL injection above) is trivially reversed with rainbow tables or brute force, and identical passwords produce identical hashes. The comparison is also a non-constant-time string equality. This affects all authentication via views.index (views.py:41).
findings.evidence: return self.pwd_hash == md5(password.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()  (user.py:41); fixtures store md5('superadmin'), md5('password'), etc.
findings.recommendation: Use a slow, salted password hashing algorithm such as bcrypt, scrypt, or argon2 (e.g. passlib/argon2-cffi) and compare with the library's verify function (constant time). Migrate existing hashes on next login.

findings.title: CSRF protection middleware disabled
findings.description: A working CSRF middleware exists (sqli/middlewares.py:25-38) that validates a session-bound _csrf_token on POST, but it is commented out of the middleware chain, so no state-changing request is protected. All POST endpoints (login at /, create student, create course, submit review, evaluate/grade student, logout) accept forged cross-site requests. An attacker can, for example, auto-submit the /courses/{id}/review form from a victim's browser to persist XSS, or trigger admin-only grading actions. The CSRF tokens are still rendered in forms, masking the fact that they are never checked.
findings.evidence: middlewares=[session_middleware, # csrf_middleware,\n error_middleware,] (app.py:25-29). The csrf_middleware defined at middlewares.py:26 is never added.
findings.recommendation: Re-enable csrf_middleware in the middleware list (ordered after session_middleware) so the existing token check runs on every POST.

findings.title: Session cookie set without HttpOnly flag
findings.description: The RedisStorage session backend is instantiated with httponly=False, so the session identifier cookie is readable by client-side JavaScript. Combined with the stored XSS finding, an injected script can exfiltrate the session cookie and hijack authenticated (including admin) sessions. There is no functional reason to expose the session id to JS.
findings.recommendation: Remove httponly=False (RedisStorage defaults to HttpOnly) or set httponly=True. Consider also setting SameSite=Lax/Strict on the session cookie.

findings.title: aiohttp application runs with debug=True
findings.description: The Application is constructed with debug=True, which enables verbose diagnostics and more detailed error/warning output. In a deployed environment this can leak internal details (stack traces, warnings) and is not appropriate for production. The value is hard-coded rather than driven by configuration/environment.
findings.recommendation: Drive debug from configuration/environment and default it to False for non-development deployments.
